title: MPEG-2 transport stream demultiplexer: 4 PID filters, packets to a ring in memory over AXI4
features: Byte stream ts_valid / ts_sync / ts_data / ts_err (one 188-byte packet starts with ts_sync and 0x47).
Up to 4 PID filters (PID_EN, PID0..3); each matching packet takes one 192-byte ring slot: words 0..46 the packet bytes (little-endian), word 47 a descriptor {cc_err, 0, pusi, filter, 0, cc, 0, pid}.
Packets with a bad sync byte, ts_err, TEI or a short length are dropped (DROP_CNT); continuity counter errors per filter (CC_ERR_CNT).
Ring of RING_PKTS slots at RING_BASE: the core writes WR_IDX, software returns slots with RD_IDX; a full ring drops packets (OVF_CNT).

fields.desc: demux on; 0 clears WR_IDX and ERR
packets lost to a full ring

irqs.name: PKT
irqs.desc: a packet was written to the ring

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: a job ended that saw an AXI error response

sequence: Write RING_BASE, RING_PKTS, RD_IDX = 0, PID01 / PID23.
Write CTRL with enable = 1 and the filter enables; IRQ_ENABLE with PKT.
On PKT, read slots RD_IDX .. WR_IDX - 1, then write RD_IDX = WR_IDX.
notes: m_* is the AXI4 manager port (32-bit address and data, 4-bit ID, no user / QoS); it passes through unchanged. Bursts are INCR, AxSIZE = 2 (4 bytes), 1 to 16 beats, WSTRB = 4'hF, never across a 4 KB boundary; one read and one write burst are outstanding at a time.
ts_valid / ts_sync / ts_data / ts_err are the transport stream input pins.
The core testbench prints one `LAT <master> dram R|W <cycles>` line per AXI burst (tb/tv_lat_mon.svh), the regression suite's latency format.
